body:
> Found 2026-09-01 by an operator session driving `french-tech-homies/pipao-v2`, asked by its human to thin a
> saturated *ready* lane before a groom pass. It had to do it as a raw `gh issue edit` label swap
> (`kb:status:ready` → `kb:status:triage`) on four cards, because hkb has no verb for it.

## Why

`hkb promote` moves a card forward — triage → todo → ready — and since #209 it sweeps a whole subgraph.
**Nothing moves one back.** The status table in `src/serve.js` is explicit about it: `NO_SUCH_VERB.triage` reads
*"nothing demotes a task back to triage — drop it on Blocked, or archive it"*, and the two escapes it offers are
both wrong for this case. `hkb block` needs a reason and records a block on the attempt history, which is a lie
about a card nobody worked on; `hkb archive` closes the issue, which is a different decision entirely.

So an operator with an over-full *ready* lane — exactly the situation `/kanban:groom` exists to address — has
one option: edit the label by hand, outside every verb, guard and record hkb has. It worked (`hkb watch` emitted
four clean `status ready → triage` events, which is a nice proof the label really is the whole state), and that
is the problem: **the board cannot tell a considered demotion from someone poking labels**, and neither can the
next session reading the card.

CLAUDE.md's fourth value names this shape exactly: *"if the answer to 'can hkb do X' is 'yes, by hand', that is
a bug report."*

## What

- **A verb that is `promote`'s inverse.** `hkb demote <n>...` (or `hkb park`) moving *ready* → *todo* and
  *todo* → *triage*, one step, the mirror of what `promote` does in the other direction. Name it once and use
  that name everywhere; `park` reads better for the operator's intent, `demote` for the symmetry — decide.
- **Does it cascade?** `promote` sweeps a subgraph (#209). The inverse probably should not: pulling a root back
  should not silently unqueue children another card depends on. Recommend single-card by default, and say so in
  the help text rather than leaving it to be discovered.
- **Refuse what it must not touch.** A *running* card has a live claim and a worktree — demoting it would strand
  both; that is `hkb block`'s job or a reclaim. A card in *review* has an open PR. Refuse both, naming the verb
  that does fit, per the error rule.
- **The web board gains the drag.** `MOVES` in `src/serve.js` has no backwards entry above *blocked*; this is the
  verb that would let `ready → todo` and `todo → triage` exist there, and `NO_SUCH_VERB.triage` should stop
  saying nothing demotes a task once something does.
- **`/kanban:groom`'s vocabulary already anticipates it.** `GROOM_ACTIONS` includes `park`, and the procedure
  hands park rows back as pre-staged commands precisely because the verb does not exist. Wire it up, and check
  whether the apply step can then include park in the batch.

## Done when

- [ ] One verb moves *ready* → *todo* and *todo* → *triage*, with `--json`, refusing *running* and *review* and
      naming the verb that fits instead.
- [ ] Its cascade behaviour is decided, tested, and stated in the help text.
- [ ] The web board can drag a card backwards through the same verb; `NO_SUCH_VERB.triage` is updated.
- [ ] `/kanban:groom`'s `park` action names a real command, and the skill says whether it may be applied in the
      batch.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; the wiki page covering the status verbs describes the pair.
goal: One verb moves ready to todo and todo to triage with --json, refusing running and review and naming what fits instead; its cascade behaviour is decided and stated; the web board drags backwards through it; groom's park action names a real command
title: hkb has no inverse of promote, so thinning a saturated ready lane means editing labels by hand outside every verb and guard
